source: SPM Essay (older format, no trial paper named) · Essay on co-academic activities
paragraphs: Co-academic activities in Malaysian schools are designed to complement the formal education system. These activities, which include debate competitions, science fairs, and quiz contests, provide students with opportunities to develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills beyond the classroom setting. By engaging in these events, students can enhance their learning experiences and foster personal growth.

One co-academic activity I found particularly interesting was a national-level debate competition held at a local school. The event was intense, with students passionately defending their viewpoints on various social and political issues. What made this activity so attractive was the level of intellectual engagement among the participants. Watching students confidently articulate their arguments, rebutting opposing points, and demonstrating in-depth knowledge of current affairs was inspiring. The competition highlighted the importance of public speaking and the ability to think on one’s feet, which are crucial life skills.

Co-academic activities like debates can also improve students’ academic performance in several ways. For example, participating in a debate encourages research skills, as students must gather relevant information to support their arguments. It also enhances critical thinking and analytical skills, which are transferable to subjects such as language, history, and even science. Furthermore, these activities foster teamwork and communication, both of which are essential for success in group projects and classroom discussions.

In conclusion, co-academic activities in Malaysian schools, such as debate competitions, offer valuable learning experiences that go beyond the traditional curriculum. They provide a platform for students to develop essential skills that can enhance their academic performance while also preparing them for real-world challenges.
